paper.citation: Aranyak Acharyya, Michael W. Trosset, Carey E. Priebe, Hayden Helm, Consistent estimation of generative model representations in the Data Kernel Perspective Space, arXiv:2409.17308.
paper.source_version: Retained arXiv transcription in Acharyya2024/prose; audit is keyed to the theorem/assumption numbering in that source.

purpose: Compare each retained source result in the 2024 consistency paper with the Lean theorem surface, clause by clause.

relation_definitions.exact: The source clause and Lean clause have the same mathematical content, modulo notation/encoding.
relation_definitions.equivalent_encoding: The mathematical content is equivalent, but Lean packages it in a structurally different form.
relation_definitions.lean_weaker_hypothesis: Lean assumes less than the source at this clause, so the Lean theorem is stronger here.
relation_definitions.lean_stronger_hypothesis: Lean assumes more than the source at this clause; this is a source-fidelity gap unless separately justified.
relation_definitions.lean_stronger_conclusion: Lean proves at least the source conclusion and additionally proves a stronger conclusion.
relation_definitions.lean_weaker_conclusion: Lean proves less than the source conclusion; this is a source-fidelity gap.
relation_definitions.different_quantifier_encoding: Lean makes an informal/asymptotic quantifier pattern explicit using an equivalent or stronger schedule/event formulation.
relation_definitions.derived_by_composition: No single source-shaped declaration exists, but the source clause follows from a checked composition of cited Lean declarations.
relation_definitions.source_repair: The retained source wording is inconsistent, false, or mismatched with its proof; Lean formalizes the repaired mathematical statement.
relation_definitions.proof_role_replaced: The printed proof-side lemma is not exposed literally; a different formal proof route removes or subsumes its role.
relation_definitions.missing: No Lean theorem surface was found for this source clause.
relation_definitions.supplementary: This Lean result goes beyond the printed source and is recorded for context, not source coverage.

rows.title: Finite raw-stress MDS objective and minimizer set
rows.source_claim: For a finite dissimilarity matrix, define the raw-stress objective and MDS(Delta) as its minimizers in R^d.

clauses.source_clause: Raw stress is the finite sum of squared differences between configuration distances and the supplied dissimilarities.
clauses.lean_clause: Acharyya2024.rawStress defines the same finite objective on Config n d.
clauses.note: Configurations are functions Fin n -> EuclideanSpace rather than row matrices.

clauses.source_clause: MDS(Delta) is the set of minimizers of raw stress in dimension d.
clauses.lean_clause: Acharyya2024.MDS is the corresponding minimizer set.

rows.review: The Lean definitions directly encode the finite raw-stress objective and minimizer set.
rows.notes: The package treats configurations as Fin n -> EuclideanSpace rather than matrices with rows.

rows.title: Nonuniqueness and rigid/affine invariance of raw-stress minimizers
rows.verdict: GAP only a specialization is formalized
rows.source_claim: Applying a rigid/affine transformation to a minimizer gives another minimizer; additional non-congruent minimizers may also exist.

clauses.source_clause: Rigid/affine transformations preserve the raw-stress objective/minimizer status.
clauses.lean_clause: rawStress_translate and center_mem_mds explicitly cover translation/centering invariance.
clauses.note: The full orthogonal-plus-translation invariance is not exposed here as one Acharyya2024 source-facing result.

clauses.source_clause: Additional non-congruent minimizers may exist.
clauses.lean_clause: UniquePairProfile is introduced precisely because distinct minimizers can have different pair-distance profiles.
clauses.note: Lean turns the ambiguity into an explicit identifiability predicate rather than a theorem asserting examples.

rows.review: Lean explicitly proves translation invariance and preservation of minimizer status under centering, but does not expose the full orthogonal-plus-translation source claim as one theorem.
rows.notes: The source uses the word affine, but its later alignment statement restricts the linear part to O(d).

rows.title: Existence of a finite raw-stress minimizer
rows.source_claim: The finite raw-stress problem attains a minimizer.

clauses.source_clause: The finite raw-stress minimization problem attains a minimizer.
clauses.lean_clause: mds_nonempty proves MDS n d Delta is nonempty for arbitrary finite dissimilarity data.
clauses.note: Lean does not need the source proof route through a bounded EDM set.

rows.review: Lean proves nonemptiness directly for the finite raw-stress minimizer set, without requiring the source proof route through a bounded set of Euclidean distance matrices.
rows.notes: The conclusion is the source conclusion; the proof architecture is different and the Lean statement is usable for arbitrary finite dissimilarity data.

rows.title: Continuous MDS over a compact model space
rows.source_claim: Define continuous raw stress by a P x P integral over a compact model space and let mds minimize it over Borel-measurable embeddings.

clauses.source_clause: Define continuous raw stress on a compact model space using a P x P integral and minimize over measurable embeddings.
clauses.lean_clause: No continuous-model-space raw-stress functional or continuous MDS minimizer exists in Acharyya2024.

rows.review: No corresponding continuous-model-space raw-stress functional, model distribution, or minimizing mds(phi) map is present in Acharyya2024.
rows.notes: This missing source layer is exactly the layer needed by Lemma 2 and Theorem 5.
rows.next_action: Formalize only if full source coverage of the continuum growing-model regime is desired.

rows.title: Fixed models and fixed queries: raw-stress consistency
rows.source_claim: With n and m fixed, a subsequence of estimated raw-stress minimizers has pairwise distances converging in probability to those of a fixed population minimizer.

clauses.source_clause: n and m are fixed while replicate count r grows.
clauses.lean_clause: fixed_models_fixed_queries_consistency_of_uniqueProfile is a fixed finite n,d theorem with an abstract random dissimilarity sequence.
clauses.note: The replicate index is abstracted to a stage index.

clauses.source_clause: psi-hat(r) is a raw-stress minimizer of D(r), and psi is a fixed minimizer of the limiting Delta.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean assumes sample minimizer membership and a fixed population minimizer.

clauses.source_clause: There exists a subsequence along which every estimated pairwise distance converges in probability to the corresponding distance of that fixed psi.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean proves full-sequence pair-distance convergence, then the identity subsequence suffices.

clauses.source_clause: The paper does not require all population minimizers to share one pair-distance profile.
clauses.lean_clause: The fixed-psi Lean theorem requires UniquePairProfile Delta.
clauses.note: Without it Lean proves convergence to the population minimizer set, showing why the printed fixed-representative conclusion needs repair.

rows.review: The source-shaped fixed-minimizer conclusion is proved with an explicit UniquePairProfile premise. Without it Lean proves convergence to the population minimizer set instead.
rows.notes: The repaired theorem actually proves the fixed-profile convergence along the full sequence and then supplies id as the source subsequence.

rows.title: Finite-model population dissimilarities have a fixed Euclidean limit
rows.source_claim: For fixed models there are vectors phi_i in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space whose pairwise distances are the limits of the population model-mean discrepancies as m,r grow.

clauses.source_clause: There are latent vectors phi_i in R^q whose pairwise distances are the limits of the population mean-discrepancy dissimilarities.
clauses.lean_clause: The active Lean theorem assumes only convergence of the population dissimilarity matrices to a fixed DeltaInf.
clauses.note: This formalizes exactly the consequence used by raw-stress stability and does not require named latent vectors.

rows.review: The active theorem only needs deterministic convergence of the population dissimilarity matrices to a fixed DeltaInf; for fixed n entrywise convergence suffices. It does not require that DeltaInf be represented by named phi_i vectors.
rows.notes: This weakens the structural content of the paper assumption to the part actually used by the proof.

rows.title: Raw-stress stability under convergence of dissimilarity matrices
rows.source_claim: If D converges to Delta^(infinity) with n fixed, a subsequence of MDS(D) has pairwise distances converging to those of a fixed minimizer of MDS(Delta^(infinity)).

clauses.source_clause: D -> DeltaInf in Frobenius norm in probability for fixed n.
clauses.lean_clause: rawStress_mds_stability_set assumes the corresponding finite dissimilarity convergence.

clauses.source_clause: A subsequence of arbitrary MDS(D) minimizers approaches the pair distances of one fixed psi in MDS(DeltaInf).
clauses.lean_clause: Unconditionally Lean proves distance to the minimizer set tends to zero; the fixed-psi form adds UniquePairProfile.
clauses.note: This is the same identifiability issue as Theorem 1.

rows.review: Lean proves unconditional convergence to the minimizer set. The fixed-minimizer form requires UniquePairProfile, which is not printed in the paper.
rows.notes: The set-valued theorem isolates the strongest unconditional statement.

rows.title: Dissimilarity concentration under the covariance-trace rate
rows.verdict: GAP only a specialization is formalized
rows.source_claim: If (1/m) sum_j gamma_ij / r tends to zero for every fixed model, then the empirical dissimilarity matrix converges in Frobenius norm in probability to Delta^(infinity).

clauses.source_clause: For each model i, (1/m sum_j gamma_ij)/r -> 0 while m may grow with r.
clauses.lean_clause: SecondMoment/Probability compile the gamma/r sample-mean mechanism at fixed type-level response dimension; GrowingQueries accepts the resulting sampling convergence.
clauses.note: The literal varying-m theorem is not assembled because m is type-level in the finite probability theorem.

clauses.source_clause: Then ||D-DeltaInf||_F ->P 0.
clauses.lean_clause: The finite concentration theorem plus deterministic-limit bridge proves this shape when the required convergence inputs are supplied.

rows.review: The finite-dimensional Chebyshev/second-moment mechanism and gamma/r sample-mean bound are compiled. The theorem with query dimension m itself growing with r is not assembled; the growing-query consistency layer accepts the resulting sampling convergence as a hypothesis.
rows.notes: The probability theorem is mathematically faithful to the concentration mechanism but has fixed type-level response dimension.

rows.title: Fixed models, growing queries: DKPS consistency
rows.source_claim: Under the Theorem 2 rate condition, estimated raw-stress pairwise distances converge along a subsequence to a population MDS configuration.

clauses.source_clause: Use Theorem 2 covariance-trace rate plus Assumption 1.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean replaces the concrete rate premise by sampling convergence and deterministic population-limit convergence hypotheses.
clauses.note: As a theorem interface this is more abstract/stronger; the literal rate-to-convergence assembly is incomplete.

clauses.source_clause: A subsequence of raw-stress minimizers has pair distances converging to those of a fixed limiting psi.
clauses.lean_clause: fixed_models_growing_queries_consistency_of_uniqueProfile proves the full-sequence version.

clauses.source_clause: No profile-uniqueness assumption is printed.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean requires UniquePairProfile for a fixed limiting pair-distance profile.

rows.review: The geometric conclusion is compiled, with UniquePairProfile added for a fixed limiting profile and the source gamma condition abstracted into sampling and deterministic-limit convergence hypotheses.
rows.notes: Under the added uniqueness premise the Lean proof obtains full-sequence convergence.

rows.title: Coordinate convergence after orthogonal alignment and translation
rows.source_claim: There exist orthogonal W^(u) and translations a^(u) such that every estimated point converges in probability to W^(u) psi_i + a^(u).

clauses.source_clause: There exist W^(u) in O(d) and translations a^(u) aligning every estimated point to the population configuration.
clauses.lean_clause: Acharyya2024 contains no source-facing construction of the orthogonal/translation witnesses.
clauses.note: Later packages have Procrustes/Gram-rigidity machinery but this corollary itself is absent.

rows.review: Acharyya2024 stops at convergence of pairwise distances and does not construct the orthogonal/translation witnesses required by this corollary.
rows.notes: Later packages contain substantial Procrustes/Gram-rigidity infrastructure, but this source-facing Acharyya2024 corollary is not exposed.
rows.next_action: Add a source-facing quantitative finite-configuration congruence/Procrustes bridge if exact 2024 coverage is required.

rows.title: Growing models lie on a compact Riemannian model manifold
rows.verdict: GAP only a specialization is formalized
rows.source_claim: There is a compact Riemannian manifold M containing latent vectors phi_i whose pairwise distances are the limiting model dissimilarities.

clauses.source_clause: Latent model points lie on a compact Riemannian manifold and their geodesic distances equal limiting dissimilarities.
clauses.lean_clause: The finite per-stage Lean theorem accepts arbitrary stagewise limiting dissimilarity matrices and does not encode the manifold/distribution structure.
clauses.note: This is enough for finite-stage consistency but not the continuum source theorem.

rows.review: The finite per-stage theorem can take arbitrary stagewise limiting dissimilarity matrices and therefore does not need a manifold. The compact-manifold/model-distribution structure needed for the source continuum conclusion is not represented.
rows.notes: This is useful finite content but does not encode the literal source assumption.

rows.title: Continuous-MDS L^p stability over iid model draws
rows.source_claim: For iid phi_i from P, pointwise convergence of empirical dissimilarities implies, along a subsequence, L^p(P x P) convergence of estimated pairwise distances to continuous-MDS distances.

clauses.source_clause: For iid phi_i~P, pointwise dissimilarity convergence implies subsequential L^p(P x P) convergence of pairwise embedding distances to continuous-MDS distances.
clauses.lean_clause: No model distribution, continuous MDS map, or P x P integral conclusion is present.

rows.review: The package has no model-distribution P over a compact model space, no continuous-MDS map, and no double-integral L^p conclusion.
rows.notes: The finite per-stage triangular-array theorem is not an encoding of this integral statement.
rows.next_action: Formalize the continuous-MDS source layer before claiming full Theorem 5 coverage.

rows.title: Growing-model pointwise dissimilarity concentration
rows.verdict: GAP only a specialization is formalized
rows.source_claim: When n,m grow with r, the same covariance-trace rate implies pointwise convergence D_ii' -> Delta^(infinity)(phi_i,phi_i') in probability for every fixed pair.

clauses.source_clause: n and m both grow with r; the same covariance-trace rate is assumed pointwise for every model.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean has the finite concentration mechanism but no theorem deriving the growing-n pointwise statement from this rate.

clauses.source_clause: For each fixed pair (i,i'), D_ii' ->P DeltaInf(phi_i,phi_i').
clauses.lean_clause: The growing-model per-stage consistency theorem assumes the required sample/population limit instead of proving this source statement.

rows.review: Lean has the finite-model concentration mechanism and a growing-stage consistency theorem that assumes per-stage sampling convergence. It does not derive the literal growing-n pointwise theorem from the source gamma condition.
rows.notes: The source proof is pointwise in each pair, suggesting a future theorem can avoid uniform-in-n concentration.

rows.title: Growing models and queries: L^p consistency
rows.verdict: GAP only a specialization is formalized
rows.source_claim: Under the Theorem 4 rate, along a subsequence the pairwise-distance error converges to zero in L^p(P x P) in probability for every p >= 1.

clauses.source_clause: Under Lemma 2 and the Theorem 4 rate, for every p>=1 a subsequence gives L^p(P x P) convergence in probability.
clauses.lean_clause: Lean proves finite per-stage pair-distance consistency for growing cardinalities.
clauses.note: Finite-stage consistency does not imply the source double-integral continuum conclusion.

rows.review: Lean proves a shared full-sequence/per-stage finite consistency family, which is useful but does not imply the paper double-integral L^p(P x P) conclusion over a continuum of iid model draws.
rows.notes: The source-level continuum theorem remains open even though every finite-stage theorem cited here is proved.
rows.next_action: Formalize the continuous model-distribution layer if this source theorem is a completion target.
